# Locality Guide: Muhlenberg County, Kentucky (1830–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 14, 1798, from Logan and Christian counties
- **County seat:** Greenville
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky, United States
- **Variant spellings:** Muhlenbergh, Muhlenburg, Muhlenburgh
- **Neighboring counties:** Butler, Christian, Hopkins, Logan, McLean (formed 1854 from Muhlenberg), Ohio, Todd
- **Economy:** Agriculture (farming), later coal mining
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist (strongly represented in western Kentucky), Methodist, other Protestant denominations

## Boundary changes
- **1798:** Muhlenberg County formed from Logan and Christian counties.
- **1854:** McLean County carved from Muhlenberg, Daviess, and Ohio counties. Elijah Wilkins remained in Muhlenberg; this change does not affect his records, but some neighbors' records may shift to McLean.
- Boundaries otherwise stable for the 1830–1880 research window.

## Available record types

### Marriage records
- **Start date:** 1802 (county marriage bonds and licenses)
- **What exists:** Marriage bonds, licenses, and registers, 1802–1912, held by Muhlenberg County Clerk
- **Online (FamilySearch):** Collection 1804888 "Kentucky, County Marriages, 1786–1965" — 3.38 million records indexed + images. Specific Muhlenberg batches: Marriage Index 1852–1862 (batch M517801), 1875 (M517804), 1876–1878 (M517805). The 1802–1875 volume (DGS 4261111) is available as browse-only images.
- **Online (FamilySearch, index):** Collection 1674849 "Kentucky, Marriages, 1785–1979"
- **Online (Ancestry, subscription):** Kentucky County Marriages 1783–1965; Kentucky Compiled Marriages 1802–1850; Kentucky Marriage Records 1852–1914
- **Note:** Elijah Wilkins's marriage (ca. 1833–1836 based on oldest child) predates the indexed 1852–1862 batch. The 1802–1875 browse-only volume (DGS 4261111) must be searched image by image for pre-1852 marriages.

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Birth registration:** Required from 1852; law repealed 1862; re-attempted 1874–1879 and 1892–1910; statewide registration with full compliance 1911–1917. Pre-1911 records are very incomplete.
- **Death registration:** Same pattern as births — very spotty before 1911.
- **Online (FamilySearch):** "Kentucky, Births and Christenings, 1839–1960" (col. 1674843); "Kentucky, Deaths and Burials, 1843–1970" (col. 1674848)
- **Post-1911 death certificates (Ancestry):** "Kentucky Death Records, 1852–1965" — complete for Muhlenberg County for 1911–1953. Children of Elijah who died after 1911 may have certificates naming both parents.

### Census records
- **1840:** Indexed + images (only head of household named)
- **1850:** 100% indexed + images — all household members named
- **1860:** 0% indexed — **browse-only**, must search image by image (NARA series M653)
- **1870:** 99% indexed + images (NARA series M593, Roll 490 for Morgan and Muhlenberg)
- **1880:** Indexed + images (includes relationship to head of household)
- All accessible via FamilySearch and Ancestry

### Probate and court records
- **Probate:** Records begin 1801; FamilySearch collection 1875188 "Kentucky, Probate Records, 1727–1990" (images). Wills 1801–1965 at FamilySearch catalog (cat. 130880). Administrator/Guardian Settlements 1834–1874 (cat. 130827). Inventory, Appraisement and Sale Bills 1842–1938 (cat. 788661).
- **Court orders:** 1799–1912 at FamilySearch catalog (cat. 130855). County Court Order Book transcriptions online at USGenWeb for early volumes.
- **Muhlenberg County Heritage journal** (FS cat. 20151): Serial abstracts of county court orders covering probate administrations not in will books.

### Land records
- **System:** Metes and bounds
- **Deeds:** Begin 1798; FamilySearch has digitized Muhlenberg County deed books (existing source in project: W8QX-B8M, Deeds 1798–1913)
- **Online:** Kentucky Wills, Deeds, and Marriages 1700–1909 at Findmypast ($)

### Church records
- **FamilySearch:** "Kentucky, Church Records, 1818–1995" (col. 2790250, 9,536 records + images); "Kentucky, Church Marriages, 1824–1995" (col. 2549562, mostly images)
- Baptist churches were common in western Kentucky; local church records may exist at county historical society

### Cemetery records
- **Online:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com); BillionGraves; USGenWeb Tombstone Transcription Project
- Elijah's burial at Gish Cemetery, Bremen, Logan [Muhlenberg], Kentucky is recorded in the project

### Newspaper records
- **Online:** Chronicling America (Kentucky newspapers); Kentucky Digital Library; GenealogyBank (Kentucky Newspaper Archives 1794–1982); Ancestry Newspapers.com
- Obituaries and marriage notices appear in local papers, though pre-1870 digitization is sparse for this county

### Tax records
- Kentucky tax lists serve as census substitutes for years between enumerations
- US Internal Revenue Assessment Lists 1862–1874 at FamilySearch (collection 2075263, images only)

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Key collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | County Marriages 1786–1965 (col. 1804888); Births/Christenings 1839–1960; Deaths/Burials 1843–1970; Probate Records 1727–1990; Church Records 1818–1995 | Free |
| Ancestry | Kentucky County Marriages 1783–1965; Kentucky Compiled Marriages 1802–1850; Death Records 1852–1965; Wills & Probate 1774–1989 | Subscription |
| Findmypast | Kentucky Wills, Deeds, and Marriages 1700–1909; US Marriages - Kentucky | Subscription |

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Muhlenberg County Courthouse, Greenville, KY | Original marriage bonds, deed books, court order books, probate files | In-person / mail |
| Muhlenberg County Public Libraries, 117 S Main St, Greenville, KY 42345 (270-338-4760) | Local history, published family histories, surname files | In-person |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort, KY | Statewide records, microfilm | In-person / online request |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives | Vital records microfilm | In-person / request |

## Published genealogy — highly relevant
- **Murphy, Nathan W.** *Early Families of Muhlenberg County, Kentucky: Vincent, Wright, McElwain, Wilkins and Jarvis.* Hanson, KY: David W. Murphy & Associates, 1999. [FamilySearch Library Book 929.273 V743m; catalog/967613] — **Directly covers the Wilkins family in Muhlenberg County.**
- Muhlenberg County Genealogical Society. *Muhlenberg County, Kentucky History and Families, 1799–1996.* [FS Library 976.9832 H2m]
- Rothert, Otto. *A History of Muhlenberg County.* 1913. [FamilySearch Digital Library; Internet Archive]

## Research tips
1. **Start with County Marriages collection (col. 1804888)** — the 1852–1862 indexed batch will not cover Elijah's marriage (est. ca. 1833–1836), but the 1802–1875 browse-only volume (DGS 4261111) may. Also search the statewide index (col. 1674849).
2. **The 1860 census is browse-only** — must be worked image by image; use the 1850 and 1870 (nearly fully indexed) censuses first to establish household composition, then browse 1860.
3. **Children's death certificates post-1911** often name both parents including the mother's maiden name — these are indirect but high-value sources.
4. **Murphy's published genealogy** (FS cat. 967613) specifically covers the Wilkins family in Muhlenberg County — consult before exhausting archival searches.
5. **Probate records** (Elijah died November 1875) — his estate administration in Muhlenberg County probate should name widow and heirs.
6. **Variant spellings** — search Muhlenberg AND Muhlenburg; Wilkins AND Wilkens AND Wilkens.
7. **Pre-1852 marriage period:** Elijah's marriage likely occurred ca. 1833–1836; the county marriage bonds (1802+) are the primary record type, accessible via the browse-only 1802–1875 volume at FamilySearch.

entry.narrative_markdown:
# Proof Summary: The Marriage of Elijah Wilkins

## Research Question

Who did Elijah Wilkins of Muhlenberg County, Kentucky (born ca. 1814; died 30 November 1875), marry?

## Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly indicates that Elijah Wilkins married a woman named **Sarah**, whose maiden surname was probably **Mullard**. Four independent federal census enumerations spanning 1850 through 1880 consistently name Sarah as Elijah's wife or widow. A derivative Kentucky birth record for their daughter Josephine corroborates the maiden surname. No original marriage record for the couple has been located.

## Evidence

### Census Records, 1850–1870 (Elijah Living)

The 1850 United States Census for Muhlenberg County, Kentucky lists Elijah Wilkins (born ca. 1814, Kentucky) as head of household and Sarah Wilkins (born ca. 1819, Kentucky) as the next-listed household member, accompanied by six children.^1 The 1850 census carried no relationship column; the spousal relationship is inferred from Sarah’s position immediately after the head under the same surname, corroborated by the three later censuses below.

The 1860 United States Census for District 1, Muhlenberg County lists Elijah Wilkins (age 47, born ca. 1813, Kentucky) as head of household and Sarah Wilkins (age 39, born North Carolina) as the next adult in the dwelling, with six children.^2 Again, no relationship column; the pairing is consistent with 1850.

The 1870 United States Census for South Carrollton, Muhlenberg County lists Elijah Wilkins (born ca. 1815, Kentucky) as head of household and Sarah Wilkins (born ca. 1820, Kentucky) as the next adult, with eight children.^3 The spousal relationship is again inferred from co-residence.

### 1880 Census: Post-Mortem Widow Evidence

Following Elijah’s death on 30 November 1875, the 1880 United States Census records Sarah Wilkins as head of household in South Carrollton, Muhlenberg County, with marital status **Widowed**.^4 This is direct evidence that she was widowed; her location matches Elijah’s 1870 household, and her approximate birth year across all four censuses (~1817–1821) is consistent with the same individual.

### Josephine Wilkins Birth Record: Maiden Surname

A Kentucky birth and christening database entry for Josephine Wilkens (born 15 June 1858, Muhlenberg County) names the mother as **Sarah Mullard** and the father as **Elizah_ Wilkens** (a probable indexing truncation of “Elijah Wilkins”).^5 This compiled/derivative record was drawn from pre-1911 Kentucky county records; the underlying original was not examined. The surname “Mullard” likely represents Sarah’s maiden name, as was the practice in Kentucky birth records of this era. Because the original record was not examined, the maiden name is treated as **probable**, not proved.

### Son’s Marriage Record (Corroborating)

The 1887 marriage record of Elijah E. Wilkins Jr. in Muhlenberg County lists the groom’s father as “Elijah E Wilkins,” confirming that Elijah Wilkins (97YZ-J3D) had a son by that name.^6 This record is peripheral to the main marriage question but confirms Elijah’s identity and is consistent with Sarah being the mother of his children.

## Discrepancy: Sarah’s Birthplace

The 1860 census records Sarah’s birthplace as North Carolina, whereas the 1850 and 1870 censuses record Kentucky, and the 1880 census also records Kentucky.^7 This inconsistency is a typical census-reporting artifact: different household members may have answered the enumerator in different years, or Sarah may have given different answers at different times. The discrepancy does not affect the identification of Sarah as Elijah’s wife—all four records agree on the name and co-residence.

No marriage record for Elijah Wilkins and Sarah was found in the FamilySearch indexed Kentucky County Marriages collection (1786–1965). The couple’s marriage likely occurred approximately 1828–1835 (before the oldest known child, James, born ca. 1830), a period covered by the unindexed Muhlenberg County marriage bonds (DGS 4261111, 1802–1851), which were not individually browsed.
